en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Eighth Chapter
Discussion on the Life-faculty:
Is there no material life-faculty? Yes.
Is it not the case that for material phenomena there is no life-span, stability, subsistence, maintenance, movement, persistence, or preservation?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is it the case that for material phenomena there is life-span, stability, subsistence, maintenance, movement, persistence, and preservation?

“Yes. “If there is, for material phenomena, life, persistence, maintenance, upkeep, endurance, continuance, and preservation, then indeed, sir, it should not be said that ‘there is no material life-faculty.’”

Is there for immaterial phenomena (arūpadhamma) a life-span, a persistence, a maintenance, a subsistence, a movement, a continuation, and a preservation; is there an immaterial life-faculty (arūpajīvitindriya)?
Yes.

Is there for material phenomena (rūpadhamma) a life-span, a persistence, a maintenance, a subsistence, a movement, a continuation, and a preservation; is there a material life-faculty (rūpajīvitindriya)?

It should not be said thus … [as before] … There is for material phenomena (rūpī dhammā) life-span (āyu), stability (ṭhiti), subsistence (yapanā), maintenance (yāpanā), movement (iriyanā), persistence (vattanā), and preservation (pālanā); but there is no material life-faculty (rūpa-jīvitindriya)?
Yes.
Is it not the case that for immaterial phenomena there is life-span, stability, subsistence, maintenance, persistence, continuation, and preservation,
yet there is no immaterial life-faculty? One should not say so… [as before]… Is the life-span of immaterial phenomena the immaterial life-faculty?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is the life-force of material phenomena the material life-faculty?
One should not speak thus …pe…
Is it not to be said that the life-span of material phenomena is the "material life-faculty"?
Yes, it is.
Is it not to be said that the life-span of immaterial phenomena is the "immaterial life-faculty"? It should not be so stated … [and so on] …
Is the life-span of material phenomena the immaterial life-faculty?
Yes. Is the life-span of immaterial phenomena the material life-faculty? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said of the life-force of immaterial phenomena that it is the “material life-faculty”?
“Yes.
“Is it not to be said of material phenomena that their life is the ‘immaterial life-faculty’?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the life-span of both material and immaterial phenomena the immaterial life-faculty?
Yes.
Is the life-span of both material and immaterial phenomena the material life-faculty (*rūpajīvitindriya*)?
One should not say so… [as before]… It should not be said that the life-span of both material and immaterial phenomena is the material life-faculty.
“Is it the material life-faculty?
Yes. And is it not to be said that the life-span of both material and immaterial phenomena [is the life-faculty]? Yes.
“Is there no material life-faculty?
One should not say so ... pe ...
“Is there no material life-faculty? One should not say so.
“Yes.
“Then for one who has attained cessation, there is no life-faculty?
“One should not say so … [and so on].”
Is there the life-faculty for one who has attained cessation? Yes.
If there is the life-faculty for one who has attained cessation, then indeed, it should not be said—
“There is no material life-faculty.
Does the life-faculty exist for one who has attained cessation? Yes.
To which aggregate does it belong?
It belongs to the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha).
Does one who has attained cessation (nirodha) possess the aggregate of mental formations?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Does the aggregate of formations exist for one who has attained cessation? Yes.
For one who has attained cessation, is there a feeling aggregate … pe … a perception aggregate … pe … a consciousness aggregate?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … For one who has attained cessation, there exists the aggregate of feeling … [as before] … the aggregate of perception … [as before].
Is it the aggregate of consciousness?
Yes. Has one not attained cessation? Yes.
It should not be said thus ... [as before] ...
Is it not the case that there is no material life-faculty?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that non-percipient beings lack the life-faculty?
One should not say so… [and so on] … Is it the case that non-percipient beings possess the life-faculty?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “If non-percipient beings possess the life-faculty, then indeed, it should not be said that ‘there is no material life-faculty.’”
Do the non-percipient beings possess the life-faculty?
Yes. To which aggregate is it included?
“Included in the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha).
Is it to be said that non-percipient beings possess the aggregate of mental formations?
Certainly not; such should not be said… [and so on].
Do non-percipient beings possess the aggregate of mental formations?
Yes. Do non-percipient beings possess the aggregate of feeling? ... [and so on] ... Yes.
“The aggregate of perception …pe… the aggregate of consciousness”?
One should not say so …pe….
Do non-percipient beings possess the aggregate of feeling …pe… the aggregate of perception …pe… the aggregate of consciousness?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is it the five-aggregate existence?
You should not say so… [and so on]… No.
Is the life-faculty (jīvitindriya) arisen by a rebirth-linking consciousness (upapattesiya-citta) partially destroyed when that rebirth-linking consciousness is being destroyed?
Yes. Is the contact (phassa) arisen by a rebirth-linking consciousness partially destroyed when that rebirth-linking consciousness is being destroyed? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the contact arisen by a rebirth-linking consciousness destroyed without remainder when the rebirth-linking consciousness is being destroyed?
Yes.
Is it the case that the life-faculty (jīvitindriya) arisen from a rebirth-linking consciousness (upapattesiya-citta) ceases without remainder when the rebirth-linking consciousness itself ceases?
One should not say so… [etc.
…Are there two life-faculties?
“Yes.
“Does one live by two kinds of life and die by two kinds of death?
“Yes.”
The Discussion on the Life-faculty is finished.
